healthy.description: Your wheat crop is healthy with no signs of disease. The leaves show normal green color and proper growth patterns.
symptoms: Uniform green color on all leaves
No spots, rust, or powder visible
Normal leaf structure and growth
Strong stems and healthy tillers

leaf_rust.description: Leaf Rust (Brown Rust) is caused by the fungus Puccinia triticina. It is one of the most common and damaging wheat diseases in Pakistan, especially in Punjab.
symptoms: Small orange-brown pustules on upper leaf surface
Pustules are circular to oval in shape
Yellow halo may appear around pustules
Leaves turn yellow and dry out as disease progresses
Pustules break open and release orange-brown spores
Severe infection causes premature leaf death
causes: High humidity and dew on leaves
Wind carrying spores from infected fields
leaf_rust.season_risk: High risk from February to April in Pakistan
leaf_rust.economic_impact: Can cause 10-40% yield loss if untreated

stripe_rust.description: Stripe Rust (Yellow Rust) is caused by the fungus Puccinia striiformis. It is extremely destructive and spreads very rapidly in cool and moist conditions. It is a major threat to wheat in Pakistan.
symptoms: Bright yellow to orange pustules arranged in stripes along leaf veins
Stripes run parallel to the length of the leaf
Young pustules are lemon-yellow in color
White to pale green stripes visible on young leaves
Infected leaves turn brown and die
Severe infection covers entire leaf in yellow stripes
Spores look like yellow powder when touched
causes: Fungal pathogen: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici
Spreads rapidly through airborne yellow spores
High humidity, fog and dew conditions
Most dangerous in hilly and cooler regions
stripe_rust.season_risk: High risk from December to March in Pakistan
stripe_rust.economic_impact: Can cause 40-70% yield loss if untreated. Epidemics can destroy entire crops.

powdery_mildew.description: Powdery Mildew is caused by the fungus Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici. It is easily recognizable by its white powdery coating on leaves and stems.
symptoms: White to gray powdery patches on upper leaf surface
Powdery coating can be wiped off with finger
Yellow discoloration under the white patches
Infected leaves curl and die prematurely
White patches also appear on stems and heads
Severely infected plants show stunted growth
Black dots (cleistothecia) visible in old infections
causes: Fungal pathogen: Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici
High humidity but DRY leaf surfaces
Dense crop stand with poor air circulation
powdery_mildew.season_risk: High risk from January to March in Pakistan
powdery_mildew.economic_impact: Can cause 5-20% yield loss if untreated
